name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with a +19 partisan lean
Incumbent Mike Quigley running with a large cash advantage
Republican challenger Tommy Hanson has shown no fundraising or outside support

model.rationale: Quigley holds a heavily Democratic Chicago-area seat with a +19 partisan lean, has over $1.1 million on hand, and faces an opponent with no visible fundraising or outside spending. Markets price a Democratic win at roughly 95%, consistent with the fundamentals pointing to a margin well above 20 points.
model.watch: Any unexpected Quigley scandal or retirement, or a surge of outside spending for Hanson, would be the main way this race tightens.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Quigley, a Democratic incumbent, is seeking another term in this Chicago-based district that leans Democratic by about 19 points. He enters the general election with roughly $1.2 million on hand after raising over $700,000, while Republican Tommy Hanson has reported no fundraising and draws no outside support or opposition spending.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Quigley's chances near 95%. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and a large financial edge makes this one of the safest Democratic House seats on the ballot, with only a remote chance of an upset.
